raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. It's spring, the wheat's already been in the ground since October, just coming out of dormancy now. I need to plan the topdress and irrigations for the wheat, and start thinking about the maize that goes in right after wheat harvest in June.

---

**My thinking, field by field:**

I've got 3.5 mu — that's all. Six mouths to feed but a couple of the kids are working in town now, sending some money back, so I'm not totally desperate for cash. Still, 3.5 mu doesn't leave room for mistakes. I do wheat-maize like everyone in the village. Been doing it 30 years, my father did it before me.

**Wheat (already planted, October last year):**
I put down compound fertilizer as base before sowing — about one bag of 15-15-15 across the whole 3.5 mu, so roughly 14-15 kg of the compound per mu. Used Jimai 22 seed, the variety the extension station has been pushing the last few years. Most neighbors use it too, it holds up well in our soils.

Now in spring, when the wheat starts jointing in late March or early April, I'll topdress urea. I usually do about 15 kg urea per mu — that's around 7 kg of nitrogen. Combined with the base, total N comes to maybe 17-18 kg/mu. The extension fellow said 15 is enough but I always do a bit more — a yellow-looking field at jointing scares me more than spending an extra 30 yuan. Last year I got around 450 kg/mu, that's normal for me.

Irrigation — I'll water at jointing when I topdress (carries the urea down), then again at heading if it's dry, and one more before the grain fills if needed. So 2 to 3 times. The well is metered, electricity isn't free, each watering on 3.5 mu runs me maybe 30-40 yuan. I won't water if it rains.

Pesticide — I'll spray once for aphids around heading time, and probably once for weeds (broadleaf) in early spring. Nothing fancy, just what the agro-shop sells.

**Maize (going in mid-June, right after wheat harvest):**
The window is tight — wheat off by June 10-12, maize in by June 15-18. I rent the combine for wheat (everyone in the village shares, costs about 50 yuan/mu), then I no-till seed the maize directly into the wheat stubble. That's what we all do now, no time to plow. I use Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the seed shop has — costs around 40-50 yuan/mu of seed.

For maize fertilizer — I put compound NPK at planting, again about one bag spread across, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage in late July. Total N maybe 14-15 kg/mu. Maize doesn't need as much fuss as wheat in our area. If summer rains come normal, I might not irrigate at all. If July is dry I'll water once at silking — that's the critical time, don't want to lose the cob fill.

Pesticide — herbicide right after planting (atrazine + something, the shop mixes it), and watch for armyworm. Last few years the army worm has been bad, I'll spray once if I see them.

Expected yield maybe 500 kg/mu maize. Last year was 480.

**Labor:** All family. My wife and I do the daily work, my older brother helps at harvest. No hired labor on 3.5 mu — wouldn't make sense.

**Money:** I think the whole season I'll spend maybe 1,500-1,800 yuan on inputs across both crops. Not huge, but on 3.5 mu every yuan counts.
